checkpoints.description: [1/2] Run a contraband lot at the quoted customs cordon

impact_assessment.why: /api/customs/resolve stayed context as prompt-driven: a scan only rolls on arrival in a security-0.65+ system with contraband held, and ordinary play almost never paired those; the snapshot quoted the cordon's name and chance but not its id, so a deliberate run could not aim at it
impact_assessment.benefits: After the campaign the captain buys one contraband lot, ferries the quoted cordon until the scan fires and dumps the lot under pressure, proving the smuggling loop and its evasion stat without touching the short gate
impact_assessment.risks: contract: customs_risk_status gains one additive system_id field and no route signature changes; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: one contraband lot bought, ferried and jettisoned through the existing engine paths
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first engine assertion for the id plus ten agent tests for the purchase, cordon jump, refuel guard, reposition hop, jump cap and one-shot/lost-lot guards, 180-step gate measurement, 2,000-step campaigns on seeds 1/2/42 plus seed 7, full suite and project gates

checkpoints.description: [2/2] Rotate the post-story fallback jump across the affordable lanes

impact_assessment.why: affordable[step % len(affordable)] froze on one slot because the twenty-step cadence repeats the remainder, so the captain ping-ponged between two systems and the megastructure policy never probed a restorable world on seed 2
impact_assessment.benefits: Post-story exploration visits every affordable lane, recovering late-game mechanics that the shuttle silently starved, while the pre-story route that the 180 gate was measured on stays frozen
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none, the jump route and body are unchanged; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: a rotation counter only
impact_assessment.mitigation: five agent tests for rotation, preserved first slot, pre-story freeze, affordability and cadence plus the 180-step gate and three campaign seeds

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Decommission a destroyed escort after the campaign

impact_assessment.why: /api/fleet/escort/dismiss stayed context because live-hull decommissioning is permanent, but every benchmark campaign ends with the bought corvette at hull zero: the repair tour requires hull above zero, so the wreck can never be repaired, never fights, and still holds its assigned engineer forever
impact_assessment.benefits: A wrecked bought escort is decommissioned in place, releasing its officer, while live hulls and prizes stay untouched and the drydock sale keeps handling captured prizes
impact_assessment.risks: contract: /api/fleet/escort/dismiss keeps a narrowed CONTEXT_ACTIONS reason and no signature change; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: one dead hull removed through the existing engine path
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first tests for the wrecked-escort dismissal, live-hull keep, destroyed-prize exclusion, one-shot guard and pre-campaign gate, 180-step gate measurement, 2,000-step campaigns on seeds 1/2/42, full suite and project gates

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Crew recruitment never reuses an id after a dismissal

impact_assessment.why: The 2,000-step seed-11 campaign ended with crew_engineer_6 duplicated and crew_engineer_5 missing: the recruit suffix comes from the roster length, so dismiss-then-recruit mints an id that is still present, making every id lookup (dismiss, station, shore leave, escort captain) ambiguous
impact_assessment.benefits: Recruits always receive a free suffix, so the roster stays addressable for the whole campaign
impact_assessment.risks: contract: recruit_crew_member keeps its signature and a new helper owns the uniqueness; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: no save-schema change
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first tests for the reused-suffix skip, the natural free index, the missing-role guard and the recruit-after-dismiss sequence, 180-step gate, four campaigns, full suite and project gates

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Vent a live reactor heat spike and service the integrity it costs

impact_assessment.why: /api/reactor/vent and /api/reactor/repair were the last never-proven catalog endpoints: the engine refuses them unless the core is hot or hurt, and the rotating tour meets transient spikes too late; a state-driven tour attempt was reverted because declining shifts the cursor and cost seed 1 the customs/void families
impact_assessment.benefits: The post-story captain vents while heat is actually present and services the purge damage at the next dock, closing the coverage frontier without moving the tour schedule or the 180-step benchmark
impact_assessment.risks: contract: no route or signature change, two additive post-story actions; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: repeated purges cost 1 integrity each and each service is paid from the post-story treasury
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first tests for the hot/cool vent gate, coolant recharge, pre-campaign gate, docked service, damage and heat triggers, credits floor and orderings, 180-step gate, three campaigns plus a full invariant sweep

checkpoints.description: [1/3] A save carries the live RNG stream

impact_assessment.why: a resume comparison showed dozens of divergences because every load reseeded random.Random(galaxy_seed), replaying the first rolls instead of continuing the stream
impact_assessment.benefits: a resumed campaign continues exactly like the uninterrupted one
impact_assessment.risks: contract: GameState gains one optional field and the snapshot never exposes it; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: the 625-int Mersenne state is stored in the save
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first tests for capture, round trip, resumed stream, legacy absence and malformed values plus resume parity probes

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Loading does not recompute live trade links

impact_assessment.why: _bootstrap_frontier recomputed the route table on every load and replaced live volumes the tick had evolved, drifting the resumed economy by a few units
impact_assessment.benefits: the route table stays exactly as saved
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: legacy saves without a table still get one
impact_assessment.mitigation: four failing-first tests pinning preserved volumes, legacy backfill, exact round trip and empty-table replacement

checkpoints.description: [3/3] Only a real pre-demographics world is backfilled on load

impact_assessment.why: legacy_body meant capacity<=0, but fresh gas giants and lava worlds legitimately have zero capacity; after a war left one unclaimed the next load re-seeded it and stamped the system owner's flag on it
impact_assessment.benefits: territory bookkeeping no longer changes just by loading a save
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: legacy saves keep migrating because they lack tech_level too
impact_assessment.mitigation: two failing-first tests plus the existing population-economy legacy migration test
